summary: notification-service is OOMKilling roughly every 24h due to a memory leak introduced by deployment dep-5402 (v3.8.0, 2026-03-21T00:00Z) which added an unbounded in-memory template cache (ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment). Memory was flat at ~48% before the deploy, then climbed monotonically to ~98% and reset via OOMKill at 03-21T22:59, 03-22T21:59 and 03-23T19:59 (restarts counter 0->1->2->3), accompanied by old-gen full-GC thrash warnings. Consumer-lag spikes to thousands are a consequence of the consumer being down during each OOM restart, which is what delayed trade-confirmation emails. The reported Kafka maintenance (retention reduction at 03-23T18:00) is coincidental: two of the three OOMs predate it, so Kafka is not the origin. Recommended fix: roll back dep-5402 or bound/evict the template cache (size/TTL), then replay the lagged messages.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Unbounded in-memory template cache (dep-5402) leaks heap -> 24h OOMKill cycle -> consumer lag/email delay
ranked_hypotheses.statement: notification-service v3.8.0 (dep-5402, deployed 2026-03-21T00:00Z) added a ConcurrentHashMap template cache keyed by template+locale+userSegment with no bound/eviction. Entries accumulate over ~24h, old-gen fills to ~98%, GC goes into full-GC thrash and the container is OOMKilled (exit 137); while the consumer is down its Kafka consumer lag spikes and trade-confirmation emails are delayed. The Kafka retention change is incidental.

causal_chain.claim: cache entries grow monotonically, memory_pct climbs from ~48% to ~98% over ~22h
old-gen full-GC thrash then OOMKill (exit 137), restart resets memory to ~48%
consumer downtime during OOM restart spikes consumer lag and delays emails
cycle repeats every ~24h producing the third OOM

assumptions: The reported 'third OOM this week' corresponds to the three events at 03-21T22:59, 03-22T21:59 and 03-23T19:59 (no earlier, pre-deploy OOMs exist).
The template cache keys grow with distinct template/locale/userSegment combinations so the map is effectively unbounded.
No eviction/TTL exists in the cache code (not directly observable from provided data).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka maintenance / replays cause the consumer to choke and OOM
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The Kafka retention change (cfg-2410, 03-23T18:00Z) / broker maintenance triggered a consumer replay whose backlog consumed heap, causing the OOM restart and lag spike.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: OOM restarts #1 (03-21T22:59) and #2 (03-22T21:59) occurred BEFORE the 03-23T18:00 Kafka change, and memory was already ramping from 03-21T00:00 (deploy time). Lag spikes align with the restarts (consequence, not cause), CPU is flat and no broker error/telemetry anomaly was found in kafka logs. Timing disproves Kafka as origin.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation: trading load outgrew provisioned memory
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Steadily rising traffic/message volume simply exceeded the provisioned heap, causing OOM without any faulty change.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Memory was perfectly flat at ~48% for the entire pre-deploy window and began climbing at the exact deploy timestamp; a pure capacity issue would not produce a sudden post-deploy regression nor a clean resettable 24h sawtooth.

facts.statement: notification-service v3.8.0 dep-5402 (2026-03-21T00:00Z) added an in-memory template cache keyed by template+locale+userSegment.
Memory was flat ~48% before the deploy and began a monotonic climb immediately after it, reaching ~92-95% by 03-21T20:00.
memory_pct follows a ~24h sawtooth resetting to ~48% at each OOM.
Cumulative restarts counter rose 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 matching the three OOM events.
consumer_lag spikes only in the same buckets as the OOM restarts (2273/790/810 vs baseline ~57).
cpu_pct stayed flat ~25%, ruling out CPU saturation.
The only config change was kafka cfg-2410 (retention 7d->3d) at 03-23T18:00Z, after two of the three OOMs.
Heap-over-90% / long full-GC warnings precede each OOM.
Past incidents HIST-104/HIST-112 are Kafka-lag-shaped but for different services and dates (leads only).

assumptions: The three observed OOM events correspond to the reported 'third OOM this week' (no pre-deploy OOMs).
The TemplateCache has no size bound or TTL/eviction (code not directly observable).
Cache keys are diverse enough that the map grows unbounded over a day.

timeline.event: Baseline: memory_pct flat ~48%, restarts=0, consumer_lag baseline ~57.
dep-5402 deployed: notification-service v3.8.0 adds in-memory template cache.
First 'heap usage N% over 90 (old gen)' full-GC warnings appear.
OOMKill #1 (exit 137); memory resets to ~48%; consumer_lag spikes to max 17161.
Kafka cfg-2410 retention 7d->3d (incidental to symptom onset).
OOMKill #3; restarts counter -> 3; lag spike; emails delayed ~25 min.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back dep-5402 (notification-service v3.8.0) to the last version without the template cache, or immediately disable the TemplateCache via feature flag.
recommended_actions.rationale: Memory growth began exactly at the deploy and resets only on OOMKill; rollback removes the leak source.

recommended_actions.action: Bound the template cache (max entries + TTL/eviction) or move it to an external bounded cache (e.g. Redis) before re-enabling.
recommended_actions.rationale: The ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment is effectively unbounded and fills heap over ~24h.

recommended_actions.action: After restoring memory stability, allow the consumer to drain and replay the lagged trade-confirmation messages.
recommended_actions.rationale: consumer_lag spiked to thousands and emails were delayed; the backlog must be cleared.

recommended_actions.action: Add heap-usage alerting (old-gen %, full-GC time) with a forecast-to-OOM warning instead of waiting for the Killed event.
recommended_actions.rationale: The heap-over-90%/long-GC warnings preceded each OOM by hours and were not acted on early.

data_gaps: No heap-used / old-gen byte-level metric is exposed (heap_used_mb not_found); growth is inferred from memory_pct only.
No notification-service code/diff or line-level detail of the TemplateCache bounds to confirm absence of eviction.
No request_rate / template-cardinality series to quantify cache key growth.
No kafka broker-side logs beyond a TLS-cipher warning, so broker telemetry during the OOM windows is not directly observable.
Whether any pre-2026-03-21 OOMs existed is not covered by the queried window (restarts counter starts at 0 on 03-20).

findings.statement: notification-service v3.8.0 (dep-5402) was deployed 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z adding an in-memory template cache: 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering' with 'TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap) keyed by template+locale+userSegment'.

Before the deploy notification-service memory_pct was flat at ~48% (03-20 all buckets avg 47.5-48.9); immediately after the 03-21T00:00 deploy it begins a monotonic climb ~4.5pp per 2h bucket (48.23 at 00:00 -> 92.91 avg, 95.09 max at 20:00).

memory_pct shows a repeating sawtooth: ramp to ~94-98% then reset to ~48%. Resets occur at 03-21T22:00 (avg 71.52 after max 97.37), 03-22T22:00 (avg 48.25 after max 97.98), 03-23T20:00 (avg 48.33 after max 98.44).
Three OOMKilled events (exit code 137) occurred, one per ~24h: 2026-03-21T22:59:50, 2026-03-22T21:59:47, 2026-03-23T19:59:21.
The cumulative restarts counter goes 0 (through 03-21T20:00) then 1 (03-21T22:00), 2 (03-22T22:00), 3 (03-23T20:00), matching the three OOM events.

consumer_lag is ~55-65 messages at baseline but spikes to thousands exactly in the same 2h buckets as the OOM restarts: 2273.11 (03-21T22:00, max 17161.92), 790.21 (03-22T20:00, max 17611.66), 810.33 (03-23T18:00, max 18137.93), returning to ~57 in the next idle bucket.
cpu_pct for notification-service is flat at ~25% (mean 25.02, max 28.01) across 03-21T22:00 through 03-23T23:59, i.e. no CPU saturation accompanying the memory growth.
The only config change in the window is cfg-2410 on kafka: log.retention.ms reduced from 604800000 to 259200000 at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z ('Kafka maintenance: reduce retention to 3 days').

The WARN log pattern 'heap usage <n>% over 90 (old gen), full GC took <n>ms' repeatedly precedes each OOM (first seen 2026-03-21T21:37:01, and 18:34:46-19:49:28 on 03-23), with full GC times growing to 6-8s.

findings.statement: Past post-mortems HIST-104 (2025-11-05, notification-service 'consumer lag spike','delayed emails' after Kafka broker rebalance) and HIST-112 (2026-02-03, settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment) show lag-after-Kafka-shaped symptoms, but both are different services/dates and are leads only.

refs.quote: Partition reassignment caused consumer group rebalancing storm

findings.statement: Inference: the lag spikes are a consequence of the OOM restarts (consumer stops consuming during/after the crash) rather than their cause, because lag rises only in the same buckets as the restarts and the restarts at 03-21T22:59 and 03-22T21:59 predate the 03-23T18:00 Kafka change.

Inference: the flat ~48% memory before 03-21T00:00 and the monotonic climb after it, resetting only on OOMKill, is the signature of an unbounded memory leak introduced at 03-21T00:00 (matching dep-5402's new in-memory template cache); the ~24h fill-to-OOM periodicity is consistent with steady allocation into a cache that is never bounded or evicted.
